chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Mus'ab ibn Salam al-Tamimi, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever calls the adhan for ten years, holding it for God's sake, God will forgive him for as far as his sight reaches and as far as his voice reaches in the sky. Every moist and dry thing that hears him will acknowledge him. He will have a share of the reward of whoever prays with him in his mosque, and he will have a good deed for whoever prays due to his voice.

key_terms.رَطْبٍ وَيَابِسٍ: Moist and dry (referring to all created beings, including humans and jinn)
key_terms.مَدَّ بَصَرِهِ: As far as his sight reaches
key_terms.مَدَّ صَوْتِهِ: As far as his voice reaches
key_terms.مُحْتَسِبًا: Holding it for God's sake / with sincere intention

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for calling the adhan for ten years in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the enduring merit of the mu'adhin, noting that a decade of sincere adhan grants forgiveness proportional to the reach of one's sight and voice, symbolizing the expansive nature of divine mercy. This tradition underscores the mu'adhin's role as a spiritual conduit, where every listener and congregant shares in the reward, reflecting the communal aspect of worship emphasized in Shia jurisprudence. The 'rwet and yabis' (moist and dry) reference alludes to the universality of this acknowledgment across all created beings, from humans to jinn and animals.
